key_insight: Taguchi-based design identified current and arc voltage as the dominant controls for optimizing GMAW joint strength while balancing weld defects via grey relational analysis.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a repeatable statistical workflow for selecting welding settings that improve tensile performance and process robustness in mild-steel GMAW.
method: L9(3^4) Taguchi orthogonal array with 3 replicates per trial (27 specimens)
Signal-to-noise ratios, response tables, and ANOVA to rank factor effects
Grey relational analysis to combine tensile strength and defect count into a compromise optimum
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that welding current and arc voltage were statistically significant at the 1% level, explaining the largest variance shares in both tensile strength and defect count.
watch_item: The optimum is based on the tested factor ranges and a laboratory dataset, so performance may shift if joint design, material, or machine setup changes.
paper_title: TAGUCHI-BASED OPTIMIZATION OF GMAW WELDING PARAMETERS FOR JOINT STRENGTH
